offending_extra_words: The indemnifying Party shall not settle a claim in a manner that imposes a non-monetary obligation on, or admits liability or wrongdoing of, the indemnified Party without its prior written consent.
The indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense.

If a claim under Section 20.1(a) arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing item. If neither remedy is commercially practicable within a reasonable period, either Party may terminate the affected item and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for it and, for a paid-up licence or accepted Deliverable, the Fees paid for it.

Vendor's obligation under Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, combination of the Services or Deliverables with materials not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not have arisen but for the combination, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Vendor.
reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: Vendor defence/indemnity for IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused data incident and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, notice-control-cooperation procedure, and a Customer indemnity limited to Customer content and Customer's breach of law.

Minimality fails: the insertion imports fallback-only material (exclusions in 20.2 and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in 20.5), adds hold-harmless language, and adds settlement-consent and separate-counsel mechanics beyond the preferred procedure.
Fallback is not independently complete because no 3× annual fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity is inserted (and levels may not be mixed).
Heading anchoring places the new Section 20 heading immediately after an existing section heading rather than after that section's final body paragraph, a drafting-placement defect.
Intent is preserved: cross-references in 9.3 and 21.3 now resolve, no undefined terms are introduced, and untouched commercial terms remain effective.
